text:
deploy-bot: Deploy completed for canary subset (service: inference-proxy, version: v2.13.0-canary)
runbook-bot: Post-deploy smoke checks started: tinyprobe x50, kvprobe x20, prefix-synth x10
sara: seeing higher 5xx rate on tinyprobe in eu-west1, p95 ~ 480ms -> baseline 220ms
jon: logs from eu-west1 host-117:
```
WARN inference-proxy worker0: prefix-cache miss spike 2026-03-23T15:02:10Z
ERROR tinyprobe/handler.go: timeout calling /healthz (ctx deadline exceeded)
```
kyle: can you paste the raw synthetic output? curious if it's latency-only or 5xx
jon: raw probe snippet:
```
{"probe":"tinyprobe","region":"eu-west1","status":"500","latency_ms":482}
{"probe":"tinyprobe","region":"eu-west1","status":"200","latency_ms":210}
```
sre-lead: pattern looks intermittent, only eu-west1, no other regions. Recommend: HOLD rollout, pin canary to prior model variant (v2.12.8) on eu-west1, increase synthetic sampling to 5m window.
sara: ++ on hold. I'll open a PIN request and run the pin script
sara: `/scripts/pin-deploy --service inference-proxy --region eu-west1 --version v2.12.8 --reason "tinyprobe 5xx spike postdeploy"`
deploy-bot: Action: canary traffic frozen for eu-west1 by @sara. Notifying release manager.
runbook-bot: Runbook: https://redwood-internal/runbooks/postdeploy-smoke-checks#tinyprobe
kyle: quick healthcheck curl:
```
curl -sS -D - https://eu-west1.inference.internal/healthz | head -n 20
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
X-Service-Version: v2.12.8
```
jon: after pin applied, minute-by-minute samples look better, p95 down to 230ms, 500s gone in last 10 samples
sre-lead: Good. Action items: 1) keep canary frozen for 30m, 2) ramp monitoring sampling to 2x for 30m, 3) verify no regression in embeddings route (route: /v1/embeds)
sara: I'll coordinate the 30m hold and update release notes: "Rolled back eu-west1 canary to v2.12.8 after tinyprobe spike; continuing observation."
kyle: tagging @oncall in case error resurfaces :rotating_light:
jon: adding quick alert override to suppress noisy paging while we observe (alert-channel: eng-releases)
sre-lead: if we stay stable for 30m, we'll resume staggered rollout with reduced batch size. If spike returns, prepare rollback of full canary and open incident.
sara: thanks team. I'll post a short postmortem if we need to escalate. :thumbsup:
